full_judgment: 11. The plaintiffs' definite case is that out of their six brothers, Fazar Ali died, leaving the remaining five brothers. While Rekmat Ali died; leaving two sons, Saman Munshi and Isa Ali, and two daughters, Laxi Bibi and Maleka Bibi. Meher Ali, Yad Ali, Hazari, Fazar Ali, Poizari and the son of Rekmat Ali, i.e., lsa Ali, sold the disputed land by a registered deed dated 30-3-1972 to Sadek Ali, Mazibur Rahman, and plaintiff No. 2. Subsequently Mazibur Rahman transferred his five decimals of land in favour of his wife Rahatun Nessa by a Heb-bil-Ewaz deed who sold the same by a registered deed dated 12-5-1988 to plaintiff No. 1. Sadek Ali sold five decimals of land to plaintiff No. 1 by registered deed dated 16-6-1992. Accordingly, the plaintiff became the owner and possessor of the suit land by purchase. The Government claims that the suit land was rightly recorded in its name during the RS operation. But the Government could not substantiate any document under what facts and circumstances its name has been recorded in the RS Khatian. Both the courts below found plaintiffs' rights, title, interest, and possession over the suit land. In a suit for declaration of title the Trial Court dismissed the suit only on the point of defect of parties. On a bare reading of the judgment of the Trial Court, it is not found under what circumstances the suit was bad for defect of parties or who were left out at the time of framing of the suit. The concurrent findings of both the courts below regarding the possession of the plaintiffs appear reasonable based on evidence. The plaintiffs mutating their names and paying rents have been possessing the suit land. By producing oral evidence, the plaintiffs have been availed to prove the cause of action for filing the suit. On a careful examination of the Exhibited documents namely CS Khatian Exhibit-1, SA Khatian Exhibit-2, rent receipts Exhibit-3 series, deeds dated 30-3-1972, 18-8-1980, 12-5-1988 and 16-6-1993 Exhibits-4, 4(1), 4(b) and 5. It appears that the plaintiffs could prove their chain of title and possession over the suit land vis-a-vis there is no reason to record the suit land in the RS Khatian during RS operation in the name of the Government simply because the Government failed to produce any single paper or document showing its title in the suit land. During the trial, the defendant totally failed to produce the names of the necessary parties in the suit. So, according to Order I, rule 9 regarding misjoinder and non-joinder of parties, the defendant failed to establish its case. From the veracity of the plaint, it appears that the plaintiff claimed title over the suit land only against the defendant's Government. So, there should not be any question of defect of parties, and, as such, the Trial Court, without considering the provisions of law and facts, erroneously dismissed the suit on the point of defect of parties. As a final court of fact, the appellate Court rightly reversed the finding of the trial Court, which need not be interfered with by this Court sitting on revisional jurisdiction.
